# Shared agent result contract, application schema 1

This is an offline application contract owned by `internal/agentresult`. Current
runner, submission and publication routes are unchanged. The normative structural
schema is `docs/schemas/agent-result-v1.json`, generated by `JSONSchema` from the
Go wire types. `docs/schemas/agent-result-snapshot-v1.json` separately defines
factory-assembled snapshots through `SnapshotJSONSchema`. Go additionally enforces scope, graph, evidence and byte limits.
The executable corpus is `internal/agentresult/testdata/v1`.

## Ownership and independent versions

An authored creation is exactly `{ "result": { ... } }`. The factory separately
supplies `Context`; an assembled snapshot is `{ "meta": { ... }, "result": ... }`.
Metadata includes schema version, task, run and attempt, selected mode, logical
result ID and positive result revision. Scope/request and workflow/submission
versions are included when applicable. Metadata is attribution, never a bearer
capability. Authored metadata, answers, approval, acceptance, publication,
capabilities and execution telemetry are forbidden, including unknown nested fields.

Application `schema_version` is integer **1** and selects this format. Unknown
versions reject without migration. Result revision starts at **1** and advances
independently for each retained update. Submission contract version **2** describes
the existing contribution protocol. Workflow **1** retains legacy verified
engineering plus assessment; workflow **2** separates Implement and Validate.
Neither completion nor an advisory recommendation changes the selected mode,
readiness, acceptance, issue state or publication.

## Strict creation and diagnostics

`Create(bytes, context)` returns a candidate only after complete structural and
semantic validation. `Decode` rejects malformed/trailing JSON, duplicate object
keys, unknown fields, wrong types, null at every location and invalid UTF-8.
`MaxBytes` is the existing 4 MiB contribution ceiling; exactly that size is
permitted. `MaxDepth` is 32 nested containers (the root counts as one); the next
container rejects before descent. The byte ceiling is checked before decoding.
No value or capability is echoed in diagnostics; unknown member names are masked.

Diagnostics are sorted by path then code, with expected/actual type where useful
and a correction. A syntax/depth/size interruption has `complete=false` and
`unchecked_paths`; it cannot mean valid input. Unknown fields can be traversed
without interpreting them, allowing additional structural diagnostics. Semantic
validation is skipped when decoding cannot yield a structurally valid value.

`ValidateResult` is the pure complete-result semantic gate; typed values arriving
from another boundary must first use `Decode`/`Create` for wire presence and type
checks. `Clone` and `Assemble` copy nested boundary values. The factory owns
allocation, revision ordering and durable compare-and-record; assembly grants none.

## Common content

Every result requires `outcome`, a nonblank `comment`, and exactly one `payload`
matching the trusted mode: research, plan, implement, validate or spike. Completed
has no reason; incomplete and blocked require a nonblank reason. Unused optional
members are omitted, never null. There are no auxiliary classification,
scheduling or conflict variants.

Questions use stable `id`, nonblank `text`, optional options `{id,text}`, and an
optional `recommended_option` referencing an existing option. IDs are unique
within their collection. Only unfinished Research/Plan results with trusted
permission may contain questions. Owner answers are never writable.

Recommendation is `{text, action?}`; text is nonblank and the only action is
`action.moveto.planmode`. Artifacts have stable ID, kind and a clean rooted
relative path, with optional description. Absolute paths, traversal, backslashes,
NUL and colon syntax reject. A path never proves immutable evidence; resolving
it requires the factory's rooted, symlink-refusing stable-read boundary.

## Mode payloads and completion

Research requires request; optional findings have stable IDs, text and source
references `{path,line?,revision?}`. Decisions and assumptions have stable IDs and
text. Spike requires request and optionally work_done, findings, decisions and
not_done string lists. Unfinished exits need no fabricated successful work.

Plan can begin with optional context or stories. Every supplied rough story needs
key, title and user_story.want. Criteria and tasks use existing typed content;
each supplied graph reference must resolve, with unique IDs and no cycles.
External dependencies and task roles must belong to trusted scope. Completed
Plan passes `planbrief.TypedPlan.Validate`, preserving complete summary, intent,
user-story fields, criteria, tasks, architecture, dependency and byte obligations.
Incomplete drafts cannot bypass that gate merely by changing outcome.

Implement references authorized frozen story selectors and retained evidence.
Workflow 2 story outcomes are engineering_complete, blocked or invalidated;
workflow 1 uses verified, blocked or invalidated. Existing `agent.ParseContribution`
checks snapshot/check attribution, executed/passed facts and legacy assessments.
Separated Implement rejects assessments. Completed requires selected engineering
obligations, allowing factory-confirmed prior completion, plus aggregate proof
when required by trusted context. An aggregate reference needs a trusted resolver;
its absence is explicitly incomplete inspection. Aggregate evidence is not
established by authored passed flags or a path.

Validate stories contain story, snapshot_id, complete criteria and review findings
in the existing reference-only assessment shape. Complete findings may be unmet
or unverified; complete assessment is not acceptance. The existing contribution
validator enforces coverage, evidence explanations, snapshot/check attribution
and code/architecture/plan reviews. Empty incomplete/blocked payloads require no
invented assessment or execution. Capture and execution are not exposed here.

## History and receipt boundary

The factory retains immutable full revisions with run/attempt attribution,
immutable request bytes/correlation and separate receipt observations. Authored
updates cannot mutate reports, frozen requirements, retained checks or previous
assessments. Input receipt/acceptance, engineering, acceptance decision and
publication/remote effects remain independent; pending never means completed.
Exact retries return original outcomes without reapplication. Same-mode authorized
context continuation retains identity; changed mode/frozen scope starts a new
result. Fresh authority revokes earlier writers. Historical access grants no write.

Sparse updates, persistence and progress are implemented by their separately
scoped APIs; creation does not perform lifecycle transitions or durable writes.

## Atomic updates and scoped reads (application 1)

`DecodeUpdate` accepts `{expected_revision, operations}`. The normative update
shape is `docs/schemas/agent-result-update-v1.json`, exposed as copied bytes by
`UpdateJSONSchema` and mirrored in the executable corpus. The contribution byte ceiling
and depth 32 apply before interpretation; `MaxOperations` permits 1 through 256
ordered operations. Operation `op` is exactly `set`, `remove`, `add_item`,
`update_item`, `remove_item` or `reorder`. Unknown/null members reject.

A target is `{field, story?, id?}`. `field` is one of the exact names below,
not an executable path or JSON Pointer; numeric indexing is unsupported. `story`
is required only for fields nested below `payload.plan.stories`. `id` selects a
collection-local stable identity (`id`, story `key`, or frozen `story` reference).
It is required for item add/update/remove and absent for set/remove/reorder.

| Mode | Maximum editable fields in addition to common fields |
| --- | --- |
| All | `outcome`, `comment`, `reason`, `recommendation`, `questions`, `artifacts` |
| Research | `payload.research.request`, `.findings`, `.decisions`, `.assumptions` |
| Plan | `payload.plan.summary`, `.context`, `.stories`; nested story `.title`, `.intent`, `.user_story`, `.acceptance_criteria`, `.tasks`, `.architecture`, `.dependencies` |
| Implement | `payload.implement.stories`, `.aggregate_checks`, `.return_allocation` (coordinator routing advice only) |
| Validate | `payload.validate.stories` |
| Spike | `payload.spike.request`, `.work_done`, `.findings`, `.decisions`, `.not_done` |

In this table abbreviated names expand under the immediately preceding mode or
story prefix. `EditTargets(mode)` returns the complete exact names. Factory grants
can restrict each field to one parent story and/or item. Empty grants deny all
access. A requested collection cannot broaden an item grant, nor can a nested
parent selection broaden a different story grant. Draft Plan grants are supplied
only before requirements are frozen. Frozen requirements, retained file/check
bytes, previous assessment snapshots, owner answers and factory decisions are
outside this editable result. Implement/Validate values can change authored
references, never the referenced immutable proof. Current trusted context and
existing validators recheck reference authorization. Validate prepares a new
revision; it cannot overwrite the historical baseline assessment.

`set` recursively merges supplied object members, replaces scalars and replaces
explicit arrays. Omission preserves content. `[]` clears an editable collection
only when final validation allows it. `remove` deletes an existing optional
editable field; absent and required fields reject. Item operations apply only
to struct collections with stable identities; Spike string arrays use set.
`add_item` appends a complete item whose identity equals the unused selector.
`update_item` merges supplied fields of an existing item and rejects changing
its identity. `remove_item` deletes and retires identity. `reorder` supplies
`order` containing every current identity exactly once, including an explicit
empty array for an empty collection. Other operations omit `order`; removal
operations omit `value`.

`ApplyUpdate(snapshot, retiredIDs, input, context, authorizedTargets)` clones
result and retirement history, structurally checks every operation, and validates
the complete final result only after all operations. Coordinated graph edits may
therefore temporarily leave semantic references unresolved. Invalid unchanged
siblings, forbidden fields, missing proof, cycles and invalid completeness reject
the whole candidate. Removal through object/array replacement retires identities
as well; reusing retired child identities through a whole-parent replacement
also rejects. Retirement keys are opaque collection paths; callers persist them
unchanged. Failed operations expose an index and authorized typed target; unsafe
unauthorized selectors are omitted. Diagnostics expose expected/current revisions.
A stale update includes only targets the caller is authorized to inspect.

A valid candidate increments revision exactly once without changing metadata
attribution; the history service supplies fresh trusted source attribution before
recording. Pure preparation itself writes nothing. Invalid updates return no
candidate or retirement changes. Returned content shares no mutable references
with baseline, operations, or retained retirement history.

`Project(snapshot, selections, authorizedTargets, context)` returns result ID,
full-result revision and copied selected JSON with its exact selectors. Nested
story identity is in `target.story`; item identity and relevant evidence references
remain in the selected value. It does not expand references or confer file access.
`complete_snapshot` is always false. Projections cannot be treated as complete
snapshots or bypass creation/final merged validation. Historical read access and
write grants must be separately derived by the factory.

## Continuing results, immutable history and direct service

The additive `application_result_*` tables in migration 0040 are independent of
v2 managed contribution admission. `store.BindResultAttempt` checks a real running
run's task and mode. Research and Spike require no fabricated managed generation.
The factory supplies work-context identity and independent schema/workflow/
submission versions. A normalized digest of work-context identity, versions and
exact selected frozen story key/revision pairs identifies the continuing result.
Mutable Plan draft content is excluded. A changed mode or frozen scope gets a new
result identity. Fresh task authority revokes older application writers; replaying
a revoked binding cannot reactivate it.

Every accepted revision retains complete snapshot bytes, their hash, retired-key
state, source run/attempt and request attribution. Creation begins at revision 1.
`RecordResult` checks binding, context and expected revision inside its transaction,
then atomically appends the request, input observations, snapshot and retirement
state and advances the revision once. Failure rolls back all writes. Historical
revisions, frozen requirements, run reports, checks and assessment snapshots are
never patched by this service. Bound readers retrieve exact older revisions.

Requests retain exact bytes/hash, correlation and diagnostics immutably. Input
correlation is unique within its source run and must preserve original attempt,
result identity and exact bytes. Exact retry returns its original applied revision
and receipt even after later revisions, writer revocation or reopen. Changed bytes
under the same correlation reject; corrected input needs fresh correlation.
Stale revision and bad-authority submissions write nothing. A semantically rejected
submission may retain a complete received/rejected receipt with no applied revision;
it cannot manufacture partial result state or proof. Preflight retains nothing.

`turn.BindAgentResultService` is an unwired in-process factory API. Its trusted
resolver runs at binding and again for every preflight/submission, including fresh
retained-evidence reads. It rechecks exact frozen context identity; a changed scope
requires fresh binding. The service composes creation for an empty history and
explicit updates once a snapshot exists. It copies read/edit grants and stamps
fresh metadata/correlation on accepted candidate snapshots. `Preflight` returns
complete or incomplete diagnostics without allocating requests, accepted proof,
revisions or observations. `Submit` validates again; exact historical retries
recover before current-writer validation. `Read` returns only authorized projections.
`Receipt` reads independent durable observations. `OpenAgentResultReader` reconnects
historical access after restart without acquiring write or observation authority.

Each receipt has append-only attributed observations and a derived latest view.
`received` acknowledges receipt of bytes; `input=accepted` means application input
was retained, not engineering completion or acceptance. Engineering, acceptance
and publication/remote effects remain separate and initially **pending**. The
factory-only observation API can record separately established facts; it changes
no workflow table, readiness, issue state or external effect. Rejected input cannot
observe successful decisions; separated Implement cannot observe acceptance.
Revoked/read-only attempts cannot append observations. Later observations never
erase earlier entries. A factory-owned optional association can reference a same-
run/same-task v2 receipt without changing it.

The new tables reuse private v2 hash and state vocabulary helpers while retaining
public v2 semantics. New application requests never enter `ListPendingSubmissions`,
start recovery, dispatch runners, alter readiness, close issues or publish. Tests
exercise real temporary SQLite databases, concurrency, transaction-fault rollback,
reopen, revoked-reader replay, independent states and existing v2 regressions.
These offline tests do not establish live adapter adoption or provider provenance.

## Exact aggregate evidence and aggregate-only recovery

Migration 0041 adds first-class immutable aggregate snapshots and execution/check
associations. They bind application result ID, parent/work context, exact selected
story key/revision pairs and their digest, final complete-file manifest, source
run/attempt, check IDs, execution IDs and factual executed/passed outcomes. Missing
revision identity is invalid. Selected sets are normalized for comparison; changing
a requirement revision or selection cannot reuse the prior context's proof.

`agent.NewAggregateCapture` sorts and copies complete file bytes, reuses
`SnapshotDigest`/`StoryDigest` and safe-path rules, and serializes supplied execution
facts. It never runs a check, invents passed/executed flags or supplies a missing
execution-time digest. Named existing limits bound files/checks at 256, raw captured
file bytes at `MaxStoryEventBytes`, and each check's evidence at 16,384 bytes.
Failed and unexecuted facts remain explicitly failed/unexecuted. Their retention
never grants completion. `AggregateReference` returns copied snapshot/check IDs
without capturing bytes, executing commands or proving reference validity.

`RetainAgentResultAggregate` requires current Implement authority and an authorized
`git.Worktree`. Before retaining it compares captured bytes through the existing
rooted, symlink-refusing stable-read boundary. Every current changed path must be
covered, including both sides of a rename; unresolved conflicts reject. Git status
is rechecked after byte comparison. No transaction spans worktree I/O. Store then
rechecks authority and atomically retains the snapshot plus every check. Existing
scoped story-check identities cannot be relabelled as aggregate checks. The factory
stamps source run/attempt and exact scope; check outcomes remain agent-reported
execution facts rather than independently certified provider provenance.

`ResultAggregateValidator` is a fresh read-only resolver suitable for
`Context.AggregateValidator`. It requires the exact authorized frozen set/context,
all referenced aggregate checks exactly once, and each check executed/passed against
the retained final digest with the same source attribution. Missing, failed,
unexecuted, misattributed, wrong-set/revision/context, partial-check and stale-byte
proof rejects. Authored passed flags, mutable paths and a story-only check reference
cannot replace retained aggregate facts. Callers set `RequireAggregate` independently
from merely installing this resolver.

`ValidateAgentResultCompletion` is an unwired direct engineering check. It resolves
selected earlier checkpoints through store, refusing conflicted, invalidated,
superseded or wrong-revision proof. It preserves legacy verified engineering plus
complete assessment obligations, while separated Implement establishes no acceptance.
It then applies complete result semantics and requires exact retained aggregate
proof against final worktree bytes. Incomplete/blocked exits demand no fabricated
successful checkpoints. Terminal save remains a separate factory gate.

Aggregate-only recovery retains a fresh final snapshot/check association under the
fresh authorized run/attempt while reusing earlier successful scoped checkpoints.
It creates no story contribution or engineering event and never overwrites older
snapshot/check/assessment bytes. Validate uses retained references and historical
reader authority only; the capture/retention boundary rejects Validate mode and no
aggregate API supplies a command executor. New associations create no acceptance,
closure, readiness, publication or live routing path.

## Advisory progress (application v1)

`ReduceProgress` accepts separate `AdvisoryProgress{sequence,message}` content and
factory-owned `ProgressBinding{RunID,Attempt,Active}`. Sequence is positive, message
is nonblank valid UTF-8, and the named limit is 2,048 bytes (not characters). Every
response includes run/attempt/sequence attribution and a disposition: `accepted`,
`replayed`, `stale` or `rejected`, with a bounded diagnostic code on rejection.
The factory supplies current authority on every call and revokes `Active` when an
attempt ends or is superseded. A fresh authorized run/attempt starts new ordering
and count state; historical attribution alone does not authorize updates.

Sequences may have gaps. The highest accepted sequence is the only visible message.
The last 32 accepted sequence/SHA-256 identities support exact replay as a no-op and
reject changed content under a retained sequence. Unseen older sequences, including
evicted identities, are stale and ignored. At most 1,024 distinct updates are
accepted per attempt; further new content rejects with `update_limit`, while a
retained exact replay still succeeds without increasing the count. No older message
text is retained. Returned views and reducer states do not alias mutable input.

`MarkProgressTerminal` records supplied factory time; repeated marking cannot extend
the first deadline. `CleanTerminalProgress` discards terminal state at exactly
24 hours or on earlier explicit cleanup. The factory must invoke cleanup even when
no messages arrive and revoke ended attempts; cleanup intentionally retains no
permanent attempt tombstones. No timer, goroutine, sleep or clock read exists in the
reducer. Process restart may discard all progress, including deduplication state.

Progress is advisory and process-local. These APIs hold no result-store or workflow
writer, never create durable receipts, and cannot change result revisions,
engineering, completion, readiness, acceptance or publication. Message text claiming
success has no special meaning. This policy is independent of MCP or any other
transport and adds no live route.
